messages:
deploy-bot: Rollout finished for service=kv-cache version=v2.0.0 -> canary(10%)
deploy-bot: Post-deploy smoke checks started (health/probes/kv-prefix-metrics) :rocket:

maya: seeing prefix_cache_miss rate jump ~3x on canary nodes, started ~30s after new pods registered
jordan: confirmed on the dashboards — miss_rate spiked from ~0.8 to ~2.5 (per-shard) and 95p latency up ~40ms
sam: is this across all regions or a canary/EU-only thing?
maya: looks EU-west-1 canary only so far (2/3 canary pods reporting)
lee: did we change cache params in v2.0.0? eviction/ttl/priming?
maya: yes — eviction algo moved LRU -> window-lru and default per-shard TTL 300->60s (smaller warm-up windows)
jordan: that explains the rapid misses on cold prefixes. Options: rollback v2.0.0, pin canary back to v1.9.8, or run primer to warm prefixes then continue
sam: pin canary -> run priming sounds safest, avoids global rollback and keeps rollout paused
maya: agree. recommend pin canary and start background prime job to fetch top prefixes for the cache
jordan: doing pin + priming now. commands: 
```
redwoodctl rollout pin --service kv-cache --version v1.9.8 --scope canary
redwoodctl task run --name prime-prefix-cache --targets canary --script scripts/prime_prefixes.sh
```
oncall-bot: Task scheduled: prime-prefix-cache (initiated by jordan)
deploy-bot: Pin applied: canary pinned to v1.9.8 (operator=jordan) :white_check_mark:
maya: monitoring — will watch prefix_miss_rate and 95p latency, will report back in 10m :eyes:
sam: FYI change window ends in 45m. keep rollout paused until metrics are stable
jordan: adding quick release note: "kv-cache: revert eviction change for canary; priming job started" to /releases/notes
maya: ack. if no improvement in 15m we escalate to rollback plan C (full rollback). otherwise we'll attempt reintroducing v2.0.0 with extended TTL and priming instruction
lee: also add a note to the changelog about TTL diff and warm-up requirement for operators
maya: noted. thanks all :thumbsup:
